notes: Behr Process Corporation (Santa Ana, CA) is the paint subsidiary of Masco Corporation (NYSE: MAS, Livonia, MI), whose 2023 10-K reports approximately 18,000 employees at December 31, 2023. The grant supported Behr's new paint plant and warehouse in Heath, Licking County, opened April 2024 (WHIZ: whiznews.com/behr-expands-with-new-plant-in-heath/; JobsOhio metrics: 90 new jobs, about $390 million, December 2022).

Independent, family-owned ultrasonic machining company founded in Eaton, Ohio in 1971; the January 2023 JobsOhio release announced a $1 million R&D Center Grant for a $14 million expansion of its Eaton Technology Development Center. Form 5500 shows 169 plan participants in 2023 and JobsOhio lists 120 retained jobs, so the company sits in the low hundreds.

Real-estate vehicle for CrossCountry Mortgage's $46 million headquarters restoration at 2160 Superior Avenue in Cleveland's Superior Arts District; JobsOhio's own metrics list a $1 million Revitalization Grant to CrossCountry Mortgage, LLC (September 2021) matching this payment, and the June 2021 release credits JobsOhio and says the company had nearly 6,800 employees. The LLC name is not spelled out in the coverage found, so the link rests on the name, address and grant match; CrossCountry was founded in Cleveland in 2003 and is privately held.

parent: ECP Oakridge Lau Parkway Holdings, LLC (developer unidentified)
notes: JobsOhio metrics list this LLC for an Ohio Site Inventory Program spec-development grant in Montgomery County (February 2023); Lau Parkway is an industrial corridor in Englewood, the LLC uses a Columbus address, and the Dayton Business Journal reported on March 4, 2023 a 250,000 sq ft speculative building, the first in that community in 20 years, which is likely this project. The paywalled article could not be read and no JobsOhio or Dayton Development Coalition release names the developer behind 'ECP', so size is a placeholder for a single-project real estate LLC.

Venture-backed gene therapy CDMO founded in Columbus in 2020; during the FY2023 grant year it was independent, and its November 2023 release says the Columbus facility had over 300 employees (Form 5500: 298 participants in 2023). Ajinomoto Co. (Japan) agreed to acquire Forge for $620 million in November 2023, after the grant year; the January 2022 release ties the JobsOhio workforce grant to a plan to reach 400 employees.

Public company (NYSE: GIS) headquartered in Minneapolis; the fiscal 2023 10-K reports approximately 34,000 employees as of May 28, 2023. The grant supported a $100 million expansion of the Wellston, Jackson County Totino's plant (974 retained jobs, 30 new) announced by JobsOhio in August 2022.

Project LLC for the $7.5 million Ohio Site Inventory Program renovation of the vacant 140,000 sq ft office building at 1900 Founders Drive in Kettering's Miami Valley Research Park, led by Industrial Commercial Properties (ICP), a Cleveland-area private developer led by Chris Semarjian; JobsOhio metrics show the OSIP grant in June 2021. ICP's headcount is not published; the bucket reflects a mid-size real estate firm and the LLC's Richfield address matches its Northeast Ohio base.

LG Chem America, Inc. (Atlanta) is the US subsidiary of LG Chem, Ltd., Seoul, whose website lists 17,389 employees (12,943 in Korea, 4,446 abroad) and Wikipedia gives 20,000+ for 2022; JobsOhio metrics list a $1 million Economic Development Grant for 72 new jobs and $85.8 million at two new LG Chem plants in Ravenna, Portage County (October 2022), which broke ground in May 2022 per the Record-Courier. The 2023 Form 5500 count of 199 participants is for the US subsidiary only.

One of a series of Mills Barnett Sirris Holdings LLCs (II, III, IV) that JobsOhio metrics list for Ohio Site Inventory Program spec office buildings in Greene County for Wright-Patterson defense contractors; the Beavercreek address, the Mills name and Dayton Business Journal coverage of Synergy & Mills Development's speculative Class A office buildings along Colonel Glenn Highway point to that private Beavercreek developer (Barnett and Sirris are presumably co-investors). No document naming the LLC's members was found and the developer publishes no headcount, so the bucket reflects a local development firm.

Morgan Truck Body, LLC (Morgantown, PA) is a unit of privately held J.B. Poindexter & Co. (JBPCO), Houston, whose portfolio also includes Morgan Olson, Reading Truck and other manufacturers; the grant relates to Morgan's Orrville, Wayne County plant (JobsOhio metrics: 139 new jobs, $24.4 million, June 2020). The 2015 Form 5500 for Morgan alone showed 3,725 participants and Morgan Olson laid off over 900 workers at three plants in 2023, so the group exceeds 5,000, but JBPCO publishes no total headcount.

JobsOhio metrics list Peak Park Holdco, LLC for an Ohio Site Inventory Program spec-development grant in Logan County (October 2021) with a Columbus address; the name likely refers to a business park near Bellefontaine, home to Ohio's highest point. Searched JobsOhio, Google News and Bellefontaine coverage without finding a release naming the developer, so size is a placeholder for a single-project LLC.

parent: The Opus Group (Opus Development Company, L.L.C.) with Balboa Real Estate Partners
notes: Project LLC for Crossroads Logistics Park, a 213,000 sq ft speculative industrial building in Union, Ohio (Montgomery County) developed as a joint venture of Opus Development Company (ODC, part of The Opus Group, Minnetonka, MN) and Balboa Real Estate Partners (BREP); JobsOhio metrics list the OSIP grant under Balboa Real Estate Partners, LLC (April 2022). Twin Cities Business reported 206 Opus employees in 2024; Opus is a family-trust-owned private company founded in Minnesota in 1953.

parent: Cuyahoga County Land Reutilization Corporation (Cuyahoga Land Bank)
notes: Quasi-governmental nonprofit land bank created by Cuyahoga County in 2009 under Ohio's county land reutilization law, based in Cleveland (the Akron address in the 990 is a mailing anomaly); Form 5500 shows 49 plan participants in 2023, and the staff page lists a few dozen employees. JobsOhio metrics list an Ohio Site Inventory Program spec-development grant in April 2023 ($1.5 million commitment), matching the Land Bank's $3.5 million renovation of the former Mickey's building in East Cleveland for biotech tenant Verdynt Bio, which credits a JobsOhio grant (cuyahogalandbank.org/press-release/cuyahoga-land-bank-completes-3-5-million-renovation-of-mickeys-in-east-cleveland-ready-for-new-jobs-with-pending-sale/).

parent: Weston, Inc., DiGeronimo Companies and Scannell Properties joint venture (Forward Innovation Center)
notes: NEOtrans reported in July 2021 that Weston, Inc. (Warrensville Heights), the DiGeronimo Cos. (Independence) and Scannell Properties (Indianapolis) formed DROF BP I LLC ('Ford' backwards, 'BP' for Brook Park) to buy the 210-acre former Ford Cleveland Engine Plant No. 2 site for $31.5 million and redevelop it as the Forward Innovation Center. The three partners are private; DiGeronimo Companies' site lists 1,700 employees, the largest of the three, so the bucket follows it, and the JobsOhio grant (FY2024, no metrics record found) is presumably site-development support for the brownfield.

Resilience US, Inc. is the operating subsidiary of National Resilience, Inc., a venture-backed biomanufacturing CDMO headquartered in San Diego during the grant year (it moved its headquarters to Blue Ash, Ohio in June 2026). Its June 2022 Series D release reported more than 1,600 employees across 10 North American facilities, and the December 2023 JobsOhio release reports 476 retained and 440 committed jobs at the West Chester plant bought from AstraZeneca in January 2023.
